description: VERDICT EARTH is a solo-led, AI-powered Earth science project competing in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Led by a full-stack AI engineer from Karachi, Pakistan, our mission is to turn NASA Earth observation data into transparent, reproducible climate trend investigations. We combine statistical analysis, interactive visualizations, and scientific validation to help people distinguish meaningful environmental changes from misleading trends.
summary:
VERDICT EARTH — Don't just detect a trend. Test whether it survives scrutiny.

Climate trends can look convincing on a graph, but their interpretation can change with the time period and statistical assumptions.

VERDICT EARTH is an interactive Earth science investigation platform that transforms NASA climate data into transparent, reproducible evidence. Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, it analyzes temperature trends across 15,875 global grid cells using NASA GISTEMP v4 and supports worldwide local investigations through NASA POWER.

Users can explore an interactive world map, inspect historical temperature records, compare locations, examine uncertainty, and stress-test conclusions across different time windows. Guided scientific verdicts explain what the evidence supports, what remains uncertain, and how the results were calculated.

A reproducible calibration audit also reveals limitations in conventional statistical confidence estimates.

By making scientific assumptions visible and results independently inspectable, VERDICT EARTH helps students, researchers, journalists, and the public explore environmental change more critically.
details:
VERDICT EARTH — The Planet Under Investigation

Don't just detect a trend. Test whether it survives scrutiny.

The Problem

Environmental data is more accessible than ever, but interpreting it responsibly remains difficult. A trend line may suggest meaningful change while hiding uncertainties, temporal dependence, or sensitivity to the years selected.

Many visualization tools show what appears to be changing. VERDICT EARTH helps users investigate how strongly the evidence supports that interpretation.

Our Solution

VERDICT EARTH is an interactive, globally accessible Earth science investigation workspace built around authentic NASA datasets and reproducible statistical analysis.

It brings together five experiences:

1. Explore Earth — Global Climate Intelligence

Explore 15,875 analyzed NASA GISTEMP v4 grid cells across land and ocean, using an interactive world map with geographic labels, search, zoom, and selectable temperature-trend records. Users can inspect annual temperature anomalies and compare selected locations.

2. Local Investigations — NASA POWER

Search for locations worldwide or enter geographic coordinates to retrieve NASA POWER's MERRA-2-derived monthly 2-meter air temperature data. The application validates the observations and calculates historical trends, supporting interactive annual charts and temperature-anomaly visualizations.

3. Evidence Lab — Challenge the Results

Investigate how environmental trend estimates respond to different analysis periods. For supported local records, compare conventional ordinary least-squares uncertainty with Newey–West autocorrelation-aware estimates, examine time-window sensitivity, and understand the assumptions behind each method.

4. Scientific Verdicts — Explainable Evidence

Instead of producing arbitrary AI confidence scores, a deterministic analysis workflow assembles the observations, fitted trends, evidence checks, sensitivity findings, and limitations into an understandable assessment. Users can export the underlying results and provenance as JSON.

5. Guided Investigations — Science Through Discovery

Our Karachi case demonstrates why scientific interpretation requires care. The 1981–2025 and 2001–2025 estimates show similar warming rates, yet the recent period's conventional and Newey–West nominal confidence intervals differ in whether they include zero.

This does not establish that either uncertainty model is universally correct. It demonstrates why assumptions must be examined.

Scientific Validity and Reproducibility

The platform incorporates three NASA resources: GISTEMP v4, POWER, and Giovanni.

Its Python pipeline validates source data, handles missing observations, computes trends, and preserves provenance. A genuine Giovanni export is compared with POWER for the same Karachi MERRA-2 grid cell.

We also performed simulation-based statistical calibration experiments. When a proposed correction failed validation across tested error structures, we rejected it rather than deploy unsupported claims of accuracy.

Global GISTEMP cell trends are presented descriptively; unsupported cell-level statistical significance is not claimed.

Technology and Implementation

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and interactive scientific visualization components.
  • Scientific computing: Python, NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, statsmodels, and xarray.
  • Data: NASA GISTEMP v4, NASA POWER, NASA Giovanni/MERRA-2, and Natural Earth geographic reference data.
  • Deployment: Vercel, with publicly available source code on GitHub.
  • Development: Solo-led engineering with disclosed assistance from OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex.

Creativity and Impact

VERDICT EARTH combines global exploration with scientific skepticism. Its central innovation is an accessible workflow that allows people to challenge how a trend is interpreted, inspect the evidence behind a conclusion, and reproduce the result.

The platform is designed for students, educators, journalists, researchers, and anyone seeking a more transparent way to understand environmental change.

Our goal is not to replace climate scientists. It is to make scientific reasoning more accessible, interactive, and accountable.
